newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo Brazzaville militia says no talks yet.
newsitem.headline: Congo Brazzaville militia says no talks yet.

text.p: A political militia fighting troops loyal to Congo President Pascal Lissouba in Brazzaville said on Sunday it was ready to talk, but Lissouba had to admit to being the aggressor before negotiations could begin.

"Negotiations, even with representatives, have not yet started but we are ready. The aggressor has to recognise that he has committed a serious error before we can go to the negotiating table," Ambrose Noumazalay, a spokesman for ex-president Denis Sassou Nguesso, told Reuters by telephone.

Noumazalay said that militia fighters were around the prime minister's office and had secured the northern suburbs of the city. Repeated bursts of gunfire could be heard in the background as he spoke.
Noumazalay said Sassou Nguesso had no intention of overthrowing Lissouba but was trying to ensure political rights.
Officials at the presidency earlier said negotiations with representatives of Sassou Nguesso had begun.

Noumazalay said the mediation of Brazzaville mayor Bernard Kolelas was acceptable to resolve the crisis. Kolelas, Lissouba and Sassou Nguesso are all expected to be candidates in presidential elections set for July 27.
He said the action of the "Cobra" militia was understandable after soldiers surrounded Sassou Nguesso's home on Thursday.
"It is not a coup d'etat, it is not a matter of saying we are here or we are there. We simply tried to repulse the aggressors. We haven't attacked. We have only responded," he said.
He said that Sassou Nguesso was keen to take part in elections whenever it could be guaranteed that they would be fair, under the eyes of international observers.
"They must also accept to create a national army, not an ethnic army, we want a state where laws are obeyed," he said.
